title: The Gut-Health Board
seo_title: Fermented Foods Board for 6–8: Vegan Shopping List & Plan
description: A vegan fermented foods board for 6–8: miso dip, cultured cashew dip, kimchi, sauerkraut, pickled beets, smoked tempeh, sourdough and seed crackers.
hook: A board of tangy, living foods: kimchi, sauerkraut, miso and cultured cashew dip, with smoky tempeh and sourdough to pile them on.
why: Fermentation creates big, sour, savoury flavours, which is exactly what a board needs to feel interesting. Kimchi brings heat and funk, sauerkraut and half-sour pickles bring clean acidity, and miso brings deep savoury flavour.

Smoked tempeh is the hearty centerpiece. It's fermented soybeans pressed into a firm cake, and when sliced and seared it eats a lot like a smoky cured meat. Pile it on sourdough with a little mustard and kraut.

timeline.what: Sear the tempeh slices in a little oil until browned; let them cool.
Stir the miso dip together; drain the kimchi, sauerkraut and beets.
Fill small bowls with the dips, ferments and mustard.
Slice the sourdough and cucumber; fan the crackers.
Add the tempeh, dill and microgreens; serve with kombucha.

faq.a: Yes, every item is plant-based. Check the labels on crackers, breads and store-bought dips, which sometimes contain butter, milk, honey or egg.
No. Many kimchis contain fish sauce or shrimp paste. Look for one labeled vegan.

faq.q: Do store-bought pickles contain live cultures?
faq.a: Only refrigerated, fermented ones. Shelf-stable pickles and sauerkraut are usually pasteurized or made with vinegar, so look in the fridge case for labels that say fermented or raw.
